description: Trigonometry is a branch of mathematics that studies the relationships between the sides and angles of triangles, particularly right-angled triangles. It is an essential combination of geometry and algebra.

sections.title: Basic Trigonometric Ratios
sections.description: Six main trigonometric ratios are defined based on the sides of a right-angled triangle.

key_concepts.explanation: The side directly opposite to the angle in consideration.
The side that connects the angle in consideration to the right angle.
The longest side of the right-angled triangle, opposite the right angle.

sections.title: Trigonometric Identities
sections.description: Trigonometric identities are equations involving trigonometric functions that are always true for all valid values of the involved angles.

sections.title: Values of Specific Angles
sections.description: Standard angles like 0°, 30°, 45°, 60°, and 90° have specific values for trigonometric ratios that are essential to memorize for quick calculations.

steps.title: Deriving Cosine Values
steps.detail: To get cos(θ) values, write the values of sin(θ) in reverse order. Example: cos(0°) = 1, cos(30°) = √3/2.

steps.title: Deriving Tangent Values
steps.detail: Find the values of tan(θ) by using the formula tan(θ) = sin(θ) / cos(θ).

results: cot(0°), sec(90°), and cosec(0°) are also undefined because the denominator becomes zero.

sections.title: Complementary Angles
sections.description: If the sum of two angles is 90°, they are called complementary angles. Trigonometry has direct conversion formulas between them.

sections.title: Heights and Distances
sections.description: The practical application of trigonometry is used in real life to find the heights of objects and the distances between them.

key_concepts.explanation: The angle formed between the line of sight and the horizontal line when an observer looks upward at an object.
The angle formed between the line of sight and the horizontal line when an observer looks downward at an object.

steps.title: Draw a Diagram
steps.detail: Read the given problem carefully and sketch an appropriate diagram of a right-angled triangle.

steps.title: Select the Appropriate Ratio
steps.detail: Based on the known and unknown sides, choose the correct trigonometric ratio (sin, cos, or tan), substitute the values, and solve.
